Composition:
The active substance is cetirizine dihydrochloride. One capsule contains 10 mg cetirizine dihydrochloride. The other ingredients are: macrogol, 43% m / m potassium hydroxide, povidone, purified water, gelatin, sorbitol (E420), glycerol, lecithin, medium chain triglycerides, inscription ink (propylene glycol, black iron oxide (E172), polyvinyl acetate phthalate, macrogol and ammonium hydroxide).
Contraindications:
Pregnancy and breast-feeding If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, think you may be pregnant or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor or pharmacist for advice before taking this medicine. As with any medicine, Reactin should be avoided in pregnant women. Accidental use of the drug by a pregnant woman should not cause harmful effects to the fetus. However. As a result, the drug should be discontinued. You should not take Reactin while breast-feeding, as cetirizine is excreted in human milk. Driving and using machines Clinical studies have shown no evidence of impaired attention, alertness or the ability to drive after administration of Reactin at the recommended dose, however caution is advised when driving or using machines. If you experience drowsiness, you should refrain from driving, carrying out potentially hazardous activities, or using machinery.
Directions:
The active substance in Reactin is cetirizine dihydrochloride. Reactin is an antiallergic medicine. In adults, adolescents and children 12 years of age and older, Reactin 10 mg soft capsules is indicated for: for the relief of nasal and ocular symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis. for the relief of chronic urticaria (chronic idiopathic urticaria).
Precautions:
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Reactin. If you are a patient with liver and kidney problems, please seek medical advice; if necessary you will take a lower dose. The new dose will be set by your doctor. If you have difficulty urinating, you should seek the advice of your doctor. If you have epilepsy or are at risk for seizures, you should seek medical advice.

Composition:
The active substance is bisacodil. One gastro-resistant tablet contains 5 mg bisacodil.The other ingredients are: lactose core monohydrate, anhydrous colloidal silicon dioxide, potato starch, microcrystalline cellulose, magnesium stearate, talc, long chain partial glycerides, cellulose acetophthalate coating layer, liquid glucose, starch dextrin, montanglycol wax, castor oil, sucrose, anhydrous colloidal silicon dioxide, talc, titanium dioxide (E 171)
Contraindications:
 if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to bisacodil or any of the other ingredients of Stadalax listed in section 6; if you suffer from ileus (temporary stopping of peristaltic bowel movements) or intestinal obstruction; if your bowel is blocked (intestinal obstruction); if you suffer from acute abdominal conditions such as appendicitis; if you have acute inflammation of the intestines (small or large intestine); if your body has lost a lot of fluids (dehydration); if you have certain problems such as severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting or fever. These can be signs of a serious illness. If you experience such symptoms, you should seek medical advice immediately. in children under 2 years of age.
Directions:
Take special care with Stadalax In case of constipation, laxatives should only be used for a short period of time (usually no more than 5 days). For chronic constipation, you should talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. If you notice a feeling of thirst or a decrease in the amount of urine, which may be a sign of dehydration due to fluid loss and may be dangerous for the elderly or patients with kidney problems, you should stop taking Stadalax and contact your doctor. Excessive or prolonged use of laxatives may result in loss of fluids, potassium, or other electrolytes that can lead to heart problems or muscle weakness. Patients reported blood in the stool, which was usually mild and stopped on its own. Dizziness and / or syncope have been reported in patients treated with Stadalax. These events may be related to constipation and not necessarily to the administration of Stadalax. Laxatives should not be given to children under 10 years of age without a doctor's advice.
Precautions:
Stadalax should not be taken with milk. Please tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking or have recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription and herbal medicines. Stomach acid neutralizing medicines (antacids) Stomach acid neutralizing medicines (antacids) should not be taken with Stadalax so that the active substance in Stadalax is not released too quickly. If you need to take a stomach medicine, take it more than half an hour after taking Stadalax. Diuretics (medicines that remove water from the body), corticosteroid hormones The active substance bisacodil may increase the loss of potassium caused by other medicines (eg diuretics, corticosteroid hormones). Heart-stimulating medicines Sensitivity to certain heart-stimulating medicines (cardiac glycosides) may be increased due to the loss of potassium.

Composition:
One sucking tablet contains: thyrotricin 0.5 mg, lidocaine hydrochloride 1.0 mg, chlorhexidine digluconate 1.0 mg and excipients: sorbitol, magnesium stearate (vegetable), peppermint oil.
Contraindications:
The drug should not be used in case of: • known hypersensitivity to any of the constituents contained in Trachisan - sucking tablets non-haemorrhagic desquamation of the oral mucosa (erosive and desquamation changes) larger (recent) lesions (wounds) of the oral cavity and pharyngeal; • children under 4 years of age In case of fructose intolerance, treatment should not be performed until after consultation with your doctor.
Directions:
Inflammation and infection of the oral and pharyngeal cavities (stomatitis, gingivitis and tonsillitis). Upper respiratory tract infections, sore throat, dysphagia.
Precautions:
Athletes should be warned that Trachisan® - sucking tablets also contain a local anesthetic (lidocaine hydrochloride) as an active ingredient, which may cause a false positive reaction to anti-doping tests.

Composition:
Sugar, corn starch, vitamin C, fructose, Steba rebaudian extract, lemon essential oil (Citri aetheroleum), peppermint essential oil (Menthae aetheroleum), eucalyptus essential oil (Eucalyptus aetheroleum), willow bark extract cortex) standardized in min. 15% salicin 0.5%, total extract of shock flowers (Sambuci flos), total extract of marsh clover (Menyanthes trifoliata), total extract of basil (Basilici herba), total extract of hyssop (Hyssopi herba) 0.5 %.
Contraindications:
Not recommended for children under 3 years of age, people with diabetes and hypersensitivity to any of the product"'s ingredients.
Directions:
No incompatibilities with medicines have been reported at the recommended doses. No side effects were reported.
Precautions:
Children 3–6 years: 1–2 sachets per day, divided over a day. Children 7–14 years: 2–3 sachets a day. Children over 14 years and adults: 3–4 sachets a day. The duration of the cure is 3–7 days, or according to the doctor's recommendation.

Composition:
sweetener (sorbitol), ascorbic acid, lactose monohydrate, citric acid, sodium citrate, sweeteners (mannitol, sodium saccharin, aspartame), talc, magnesium stearate. One tablet contains 180 mg of vitamin C (225% RDA / VNR \*) \* VNR = Reference nutritional value according to EU Regulation 1169/2011 Indications.
Contraindications:
Do not overdo it with the number of pills taken.
Directions:
- optimal functioning of the immune system - reduction of fatigue and exhaustion - improvement of iron absorption - normal functioning of metabolism - protection of the body against oxidative stress
Precautions:
Keep out of the reach and sight of children. Store below 25 ° C in the original package. Do not exceed recommended dose for daily consumption. The product is a dietary supplement and should not replace a varied diet and a healthy lifestyle.

Composition:
The active substance is acetylsalicylic acid. Each tablet contains 500 mg acetylsalicylic acid. Anhydrous colloidal silicon dioxide, anhydrous sodium carbonate Film: carnauba wax, hypromellose, zinc stearate.
Contraindications:
Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them. Frequencies: unknown frequency - frequency cannot be estimated from the available data.
Directions:
Do not take ASPIRIN with alcohol. - if you are being treated with methotrexate in doses greater than 20 mg per week. In this case, the use of high-dose acetylsalicylic acid (anti-inflammatory doses) or the use of acetylsalicylic acid for the treatment of pain or fever should be avoided. - if you are being treated with oral anticoagulants and if you have had a gastroduodenal ulcer. In this case, the use of high-dose acetylsalicylic acid (anti-inflammatory doses) or the use of acetylsalicylic acid for the treatment of pain or fever should be avoided.
Precautions:
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking acetylsalicylic acid with any of the following medicines: - oral anticoagulants, when acetylsalicylic acid is used to treat pain and fever, if you have not had a gastroduodenal ulcer - nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs , when acetylsalicylic acid is used in high doses (anti-inflammatory) or for the treatment of pain and fever - heparin used in curative doses or in elderly patients (65 years), when acetylsalicylic acid is used in high doses (anti-inflammatory), in especially for the treatment of rheumatic diseases or for the treatment of pain and fever - thrombolytics - clopidogrel - ticlopidine - uricosuric drugs used in the treatment of gout (eg benzbromarone, probenecid) - glucocorticoids (except hydrocortisone replacement therapy), when using acetyl acid dose (anti-inflammatory) pemetrexed, in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment anagrelide - water retention drugs (diuretics) - angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists - methotrexate used in doses of 20 mg or less per week - topical gastrointestinal medicines, antacids and charcoal - deferasirox - selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (eg citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline).

Composition:
The active substances are: paracetamol 500 mg, chlorophenamine maleate 3 mg, pseudoephedrine hydrochloride 30 mg. The other ingredients are: pregelatinised starch, talc, povidone, stearic acid, magnesium stearate.
Contraindications:
Do not use Parasinus: - if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to paracetamol, pseudoephedrine, chlorophenamine, phenacetin, other antihistamines, other anti-inflammatory drugs (increased risk of allergic reactions) or any of the other ingredients of Parasinus; - It should not be used in children under 12 years of age unless instructed to do so by a doctor.
Directions:
Parasinus is indicated in: prophylaxis and treatment of inflammation of the nasal mucosa (rhinitis) of allergic and vasomotor nature and for the symptomatic treatment of the common cold and flu (for the relief of sneezing, rhinorrhea, nasal and sinus congestion, fever, headache, teary eyes, and pain in the sinuses) and for the symptomatic treatment of mild to moderate pain with various localizations: headache, sore throat, joint or back pain, toothache, pain during the menstrual cycle, neuralgia, migraines.
Precautions:
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using Parasinus.
